scope: Bazel 9.2.0 Linux x86-64 toolchain selection; no compilation or scheduler runtime acceptance
summary: Bazel 9.2.0 selects the injected adapter under the stable nonbootstrap Rust toolchain type.
Both Rustc and RustcMetadata action executables are the owned sentinel launcher.
The generated ToolchainInfo has 66 fields; all 64 fields other than process_wrapper/all_files forward unchanged, including private and callable fields.
Both actions preserve every one of the 148 default action inputs and add only the owned launcher and runtime sentinel.
The original upstream wrapper and compiler remain action inputs; all 75 generated sysroot input paths remain unchanged.
Arguments after argv[0], environment, output paths, execution requirements and execution platform remain unchanged.
Bootstrap resolution rejects the adapter and selects the unchanged generated upstream bootstrap implementation.
All aquery invocations execute zero build actions/processes.
limits: Linux x86-64 analysis fixture only; not proof for the other five target selectors.
No Rust compilation, launcher execution, Java scheduler, Codex build, remote dispatch or sandbox runtime test ran.
Exact argument forwarding is present in the launcher action's declared shell content but runtime delegation is not accepted by this analysis.
No memory recovery, process ownership, descendant control, allocation hooks or cross-platform runtime completeness is accepted.
The extra-toolchains option changes the configuration checksum, and the changed executable/input set changes action keys; these are retained in the comparison.
